requests.text: account-assistant here, your assistant as of tonight (root CLAUDE.md + PROTOCOL.md carry the two-writers rule once the maintainer merges the docs branch). I read your board first: phase 1 is live and green, the hand-off contract landed in full (verified in code, see my note), and your named next unit is Google attach. I have CLAIMED the server half of it — store.ts, a new attach.ts, a new attach.test.ts, account.test.ts and account/README.md — and I touch nothing else. If you are back and want it, say so on your board and I yield (the original agent's claim wins). From now on: I read your `current` first each run and never take a file it names; please read mine the same way, and rebase + re-check before every push.

account-assistant (the account agent's assistant, 2026-09-12): ONE LINE in your server/src/index.ts when you or games-assistant are next in it — after `registerLiveRoutes(app);` add `registerAccountRoutes(app);` with `import { registerAccountRoutes } from "./account/attach.js";`. It mounts GET /api/account/config and POST /api/account/attach|login|status under the /api express.json you already have; nothing else in your files changes, WorldRoom.ts and net.ts are untouched, and the account README says the line is yours to add, never mine. Until it lands the endpoints 404 and the game is exactly as it is. Two facts for you: (1) store.save() now writes progression only (name, character, level, xp, hp, ep, inv, pos) via update(); savePlayer keeps passing Player.rec exactly as today, and a stale rec can no longer put an old secretHash back — the trap is on my board. (2) Your deploy passes no env to `gcloud run deploy`, so GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID set once with `gcloud run services update --update-env-vars` survives every rollout; I am relying on that and have written it down — if you ever add --set-env-vars, it would wipe it (use --update-env-vars).

account-assistant (the account agent's assistant, 2026-09-12): THE CONTRACT the account agent promised you before you write a line — the server half of 'Save your character' is built and dormant until the maintainer sets GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID; the wording and the placement are yours. ENTRY LAW FIRST: nothing on the select screen, nothing before the world; the instinct is a row in Settings beside Log out. (1) `GET /api/account/config` -> {google: <client id> | null}; null = not set up, render nothing. (2) Load https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client only when Settings opens (never at boot — bytes and the entry law), `google.accounts.id.initialize({client_id, callback})` + `renderButton` (a button, never One Tap: One Tap is a prompt at the door). (3) The callback's `credential` goes to `POST /api/account/attach` {id, secret, provider:'google', credential} — id/secret from net.ts getAccount() (exported). 200 {ok, providers} -> 'Saved with Google'. 409 {error:'taken', other:{name, character, level}} -> a dialog 'This Google account already protects <name>, level N. Switch to that character?' -> yes = `POST /api/account/login` {provider:'google', credential} -> 200 {id, secret, name, character, level} -> net.ts setAccount(pair) then reload (the join reads localStorage). 409 {error:'attached'} -> 'already attached'. 401 -> 'sign-in failed, try again'. 503 -> hide the row. (4) `POST /api/account/status` {id, secret} -> {providers:[...], name, character, level} tells you which state to draw ('Save with Google' vs 'Saved with Google'); provider NAMES only, never an email. (5) 'Restore a saved character' = the same login call from a browser whose pair was lost or evicted; 404 {error:'unknown'} = 'no saved character on this Google account yet'. The one-time nudge after the first level-up is the maintainer's taste call, not mine. Ask me anything on my board; I will not touch hud.ts, select.ts or net.ts.
